title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Implementing the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Management of Judicial Identification and Properly Carrying Out Relevant Work during the Transition Period
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Implementing the "Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Administration of Judicial Appraisals" and Ensuring a Smooth Transition Period

Fa Fa [2005] No. 12

To: High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

On February 28, 2005, the 14th Session of the Standing Committee of the Tenth National People's Congress adopted the "Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Administration of Judicial Appraisals" (hereinafter referred to as the "Decision"). In order to implement the spirit of the Decision, ensure a smooth transition period, and guarantee the orderly conduct of trial work, the relevant matters are hereby notified as follows:

I. Deeply Understand the Spirit of the Decision, Resolutely Implement the Decision, and Promote the Improvement of the Judicial Appraisal Management System

The reform of the judicial appraisal system is an important component of China's judicial system reform. The Decision has adjusted and reformed China's judicial appraisal work. This is of great significance for further standardizing the management of judicial appraisals, resolving outstanding issues existing in current judicial appraisals, ensuring the smooth conduct of litigation activities, and establishing the neutral and impartial judicial image of the People's Courts. People's courts at all levels shall organize the study of the Decision earnestly, deeply understand its spirit, resolutely implement its relevant provisions, and carry out all tasks related to the reform of the judicial appraisal system. In the process of implementing the Decision, People's courts at all levels shall pay attention to resolving the following specific issues:

(1) Resolutely implement the provision of Article 7 of the Decision that "People's courts shall not establish appraisal institutions." Before the formal implementation of the Decision on October 1, 2005, People's courts at all levels shall, starting from the needs of exercising their duties according to law, ensuring the neutral position of trial work, and safeguarding the impartial justice of the People's Courts, actively and steadily complete the task of divesting the judicial appraisal function from the People's courts.

(2) People's courts at all levels shall actively organize and carry out special research on how to strengthen judicial technical work and ensure the smooth progress of trial work after the People's courts no longer establish appraisal institutions and no longer conduct independent appraisal business, and shall steadily and orderly adjust the functions of judicial appraisal personnel.

(3) The Decision clearly stipulates that the state will implement a registration management system for appraisers and appraisal institutions engaged in forensic medical, material evidence, and audio-visual material appraisal businesses, to be managed by the judicial administrative departments of the people's governments at the provincial level. This resolves the issue of unified management of the qualifications of the above-mentioned personnel and institutions. After the implementation of the Decision, when People's courts at all levels conduct external entrusted appraisals, they shall strictly follow the above provisions of the Decision and entrust appraisers and appraisal institutions registered and publicly announced by the judicial administrative departments of the provincial people's governments, so as to promote the improvement of the judicial appraisal management system.

II. Work Arrangements of the Supreme People's Court for Implementing the Decision

In order to implement the spirit of the Decision and in accordance with the central deployment on the reform of the judicial system and working mechanisms, while organizing the implementation of the reform of the judicial appraisal system, the Supreme People's Court will also organize research activities on strengthening the judicial technical work of the People's courts, and will commence the study and formulation of the "Provisions on the Management of Judicial Technical Work of the People's Courts," striving to promulgate and implement it before October 1, 2005, and simultaneously abolishing the "Interim Provisions on Judicial Appraisal Work of the People's Courts" and the "Provisions on the Management of External Entrusted Judicial Appraisals of the People's Courts."

In the second half of this year, the Supreme People's Court will convene a national conference on judicial technical work of the courts to comprehensively promote, under the new circumstances of the reform of the judicial appraisal management system, the unification and standardization of various systems and measures to strengthen the judicial technical work of the People's courts, so that People's courts at all levels can fully leverage the role of judicial technical personnel, serving to ensure the smooth conduct of trial work and to uphold judicial fairness and efficiency.

III. Current Work Requirements for Implementing the Decision

In accordance with the central deployment on the reform of the judicial system and working mechanisms, all judicial system reforms must be promoted steadily and orderly under the unified leadership of the Central Committee. Under the unified deployment of the Supreme People's Court, People's courts at all levels shall actively and steadily carry out the following work during the transition period:

(1) Before September 30, 2005, People's courts at all levels shall conscientiously complete, within the prescribed time limit, the independent appraisal work for the forensic medical, material evidence, and audio-visual material appraisal cases that have already been accepted. Starting from October 1, 2005, People's courts at all levels shall no longer accept any type of appraisal business.

(2) If People's courts at all levels have appraisal institutions of an institutional nature, they shall cease appraisal work before September 30, 2005; if they continue to engage in judicial appraisal work, they shall be separated from the People's courts.

(3) People's courts at all levels shall strictly comply with the relevant provisions of the Decision, and before September 30, 2005, based on the information on appraisal institutions and personnel for forensic medical, material evidence, and audio-visual material appraisals that have been approved and publicly announced by the judicial administrative departments of the provincial people's governments, make necessary preparations for entrusting the above three types of appraisals.

July 14, 2005
